items.title: Massive DDoS Attack Disrupts Ubuntu’s Canonical Websites and Security APIs
items.description: Canonical, the company behind Ubuntu Linux, suffered a sustained distributed denial-of-service attack on October 8, 2026, disrupting its main websites and security information services. The outage lasted four hours and 12 minutes, according to OMG! Ubuntu. It was Canonical’s second major DDoS incident this year, following a broader disruption in late April. items.title: Yandex Data Center Outage Disrupts Access to Cloud Files Following Drone Attack
items.description: Yandex has confirmed a major service outage after drone attacks damaged three data centers in Russia, leaving some users unable to access cloud files. Two facilities stopped operating, while a third lost part of its infrastructure. The disruption affected Yandex Disk users and businesses running services on Yandex Cloud across the platform. items.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks to Upload and eEecute Arbitrary PHP code
items.description: Attackers are targeting a critical security flaw in the Bricksforge WordPress plugin that lets them upload and run arbitrary PHP code without logging in. Tracked as CVE-2026-85097, the vulnerability carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and can lead to remote code execution on affected websites. items.title: LG webOS Flaws Let Remote Attackers Execute Commands as Root Without Authentication
items.description: Security researchers have disclosed four serious vulnerabilities in LG webOS smart TVs that could allow an attacker to bypass authentication, create a privileged account, and ultimately execute commands with root-level access.
